analysis:
The PR changes only the CI threat-review tooling under .github/scripts/threat_review (bedrock.py, budget_runner.py, budget_scan.py). It does not touch the provider, coordinator wire protocol, keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, fan helper, or prefix cache. I found no regression against the canonical threat IDs (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041 and others). I did not trace the review tool's own trust model, since the supplied model covers the provider and not the CI tool.

Behavior examined:
- bedrock.py adds a 'workload' call policy. limit starts at 0 and plan_calls() raises limit to min(planned+1, ceiling). Planning past the 500 ceiling raises BudgetStopped. __call__ still enforces self.calls >= self.limit (head lines 122-125). The fail-closed accounting stops (lines 204-213) and the no-fallback-on-uncertain-failure behavior (lines 174-177) are unchanged.
- The credentials-unavailable fallback (line 127-128) runs before calls is incremented, so it bypasses the native limit. It is bounded by PaidCalls' own durable caps and is pre-existing, so I did not report it.
- budget_runner.py (head lines 175-177) refuses manual reruns (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT != 1) before any paid call. It sets snapshot['finished'] on failure and adds a 'Human review required' banner for incomplete or errored scans. Incomplete scans are not rendered as cleared. A clean 'Scan completed.' banner appears only when complete is true, which requires integration, full coverage and no errors.
- The force_deep permission check (lines 185-190) is retained.
- budget_scan.py adds a finished flag and plan_calls() hooks before source, depth and integration stages. Planning runs inside the try/except (run), so a BudgetStopped is recorded as an error and the scan is not marked complete. Cached batches may cause over-planning, which is conservative.

Remaining uncertainty is limited. The budget_scan.py patch excerpt is truncated, and the workflow files that drop paid dispatch are not supplied. Neither changes any provider threat-model conclusion.
